questions.prompt: A ViT uses 16x16 patches on a 224x224 image and a CLS token. How many tokens enter the first encoder block?
A ViT uses 16x16 patches on a 224x224 image and a CLS token. How many entries does one head's attention matrix have?
Why does a plain self-attention layer need position codes in a vision transformer?
options: Without position codes the softmax rows no longer sum to 1 across the patch tokens.
Patch embeddings are too small to carry content unless position codes are added.
Position codes are needed only to reduce the computational cost of attention.
Attention is permutation-equivariant, so without codes it cannot tell where a patch came from.
questions.explanation: Shuffling tokens just shuffles outputs; spatial arrangement is invisible unless added.

questions.prompt: The image side is doubled and the patch size is unchanged. How does the attention matrix size per head change?
questions.explanation: Tokens grow 4x, the matrix grows with the square: 16x.

questions.prompt: Two orthogonal unit tokens, identity weights and d=2. What is the attention weight of token 1 on itself (4 decimals)?
A ViT pretrained at 224 px with learned position embeddings is used at 384 px. What must be handled?
options: Nothing; learned position codes are resolution-independent and transfer directly.
The embedding table has the wrong number of positions; interpolate the 2D grid.
The patch size must change to 14 so the larger image has the same token count.
The softmax temperature must be set to zero to handle the longer sequence.
questions.explanation: There are 576 positions instead of 196; reshape and interpolate the grid.
